main.title: The Simpsons: Tapped Out
main.subtitle: Rebuilding Springfield on mobile
main.summary: The Simpsons: Tapped Out was a city-building mobile game for iOS and Android based on the American media franchise The Simpsons.

cards.heading: Rebuilding Springfield on mobile
cards.text: The Simpsons: Tapped Out was a city-building mobile game for iOS and Android based on the American media franchise The Simpsons. It allowed users to create and maintain their own version of Springfield using familiar characters and buildings. The game was regularly updated with new content, often seasonal and holiday-themed, for example, during holidays like Thanksgiving, and Treehouse of Horror episodes-related content for Halloween. The game was available in several languages such as English, French, Turkish, Italian, German, Simplified Chinese, Peninsular Spanish and both European Portuguese and Brazilian Portuguese. It was developed and published by EA Mobile and launched worldwide on March 1, 2012, for iOS and on February 6, 2013, for Android. The game was released for Amazon Fire devices in several markets on June 24, 2013.

cards.heading: A long-running game closes in 2025
cards.text: According to its own estimates as of 2014, Electronic Arts generated over $130 million in revenue since the game's release. The game was shut down on January 24, 2025. A community-maintained continuation of the game was released soon after the game's closure.

main.title: Mario Party 9
main.subtitle: Everyone shares the same ride
main.summary: Mario Party 9 is NDcube's Wii party game, first released in Europe on 2 March 2012.

cards.heading: Everyone shares the same ride
cards.text: Mario Party 9 is NDcube's Wii party game, first released in Europe on 2 March 2012. Its largest change places all four characters in one vehicle moving along the board together. Players take turns driving, gathering Mini Stars and trying to avoid the losses attached to Mini Ztars. The shared position makes the contest unusually close: everyone sees the same approaching stretch, but the person currently holding the dice controls which opportunity or danger the group reaches next.

cards.heading: Take the wheel at the right moment
cards.text: The active driver rolls to move the vehicle, making a useful destination depend on whose turn arrives at that point in the route. Mini Stars are collected along the way instead of being purchased through the older coin-and-Star structure. Minigames appear through spaces and events rather than automatically after every full round. This changes the pace between the board and its short contests. A helpful roll for the vehicle may still leave a different player best placed to benefit from what lies immediately ahead.

cards.heading: The board ends with a common opponent
cards.text: Boss minigames appear midway through a board and again at its conclusion. The group fights a common enemy while still competing over the rewards, briefly joining the players around the same target. Eighty-one minigames support the different activities, and Party Points purchase additional content. Toshiki Aida and Ryosuke Asami composed the score. Mario Party 9 begins a distinct phase of the series by replacing separate journeys with a common ride, making control of the next turn more important than a player's independent position on the map.

main.title: Unit 13
main.subtitle: A tactical assignment built for a short return visit
main.summary: Unit 13 is Zipper Interactive's PlayStation Vita third-person shooter, first released in North America on 6 March 2012. Its military operations are organised as individual missions with objectives and conditions that can change the approach required. Some allow several ways to complete the task, while others impose restrictions such as remaining unseen. The player uses the Vita's paired sticks to move and aim, bringing a familiar console-shooter arrangement to a handheld. A mission becomes a compact problem that can be attempted again with a clearer plan rather than only a chapter passed once.

cards.heading: A tactical assignment built for a short return visit
cards.text: Unit 13 is Zipper Interactive's PlayStation Vita third-person shooter, first released in North America on 6 March 2012. Its military operations are organised as individual missions with objectives and conditions that can change the approach required. Some allow several ways to complete the task, while others impose restrictions such as remaining unseen. The player uses the Vita's paired sticks to move and aim, bringing a familiar console-shooter arrangement to a handheld. A mission becomes a compact problem that can be attempted again with a clearer plan rather than only a chapter passed once.

cards.heading: The same location can ask another question
cards.text: Objectives can be completed in different orders, allowing the player to judge which route makes the operation more manageable. Dynamic mode changes objective and enemy locations, equipment and other conditions, giving a familiar environment another arrangement. Knowledge of the space remains useful without making every threat predictable. All missions can also be played cooperatively, turning the choice of route into something shared with another person. The structure encourages repeated visits because a location is treated as a set of tactical possibilities rather than a single fixed sequence of enemies and instructions.

cards.heading: Zipper's final game
cards.text: Justin Burnett composed the music for a project released near the Vita's international launch. European and Japanese editions followed within days of North America. Unit 13 became the final game from Zipper Interactive before Sony closed the studio, ending a history closely associated with SOCOM and tactical console shooting. Its design carries that experience into a different format. Rather than depending entirely on a long cinematic campaign, it gives the handheld a collection of operations whose objectives, conditions and cooperative options can make a short session feel complete while still leaving another variation to attempt.

main.title: Mass Effect 3
main.subtitle: Shepard brings the original trilogy to its conclusion
main.summary: Mass Effect 3 begins with Earth under attack and Commander Shepard seeking a way to resist the Reapers.

cards.heading: Shepard brings the original trilogy to its conclusion
cards.text: Mass Effect 3 begins with Earth under attack and Commander Shepard seeking a way to resist the Reapers. BioWare's 2012 game closes the original trilogy by making the search for allies part of a military emergency. Familiar relationships are now tested by a threat that reaches beyond one world.

cards.heading: Previous decisions carry into the campaign
cards.text: Importing a previous save can carry decisions and relationships into the new campaign. The person meeting Shepard may therefore have a history the player helped create in an earlier game.

cards.heading: Squad powers combine with cover-based combat
cards.text: Combat pairs cover and gunfire with technical and biotic abilities. Teammates can combine powers, giving squad selection a tactical purpose alongside its role in the story. The original release also includes a separate cooperative multiplayer mode.

main.title: I Am Alive
main.subtitle: Climbing depends on limited stamina
main.summary: I Am Alive makes survival a matter of reading a situation before acting. Stamina, scarce supplies and the threat of an unloaded weapon turn climbing and confrontation into tense decisions in a ruined city.

cards.heading: Climbing depends on limited stamina
cards.text: Climbing in I Am Alive consumes stamina. Scaling ruined buildings lets the protagonist reach breathable air and supplies, but each handhold uses energy. Players must judge distances, find grips and look for places to rest before attempting a route. A climb can leave the protagonist exhausted before reaching safety. Ubisoft presented stamina management as one of the central survival systems.

cards.heading: An empty gun can intimidate an opponent
cards.text: Ammunition is scarce. Ubisoft described an intimidation system in which some enemies may retreat when threatened with a gun, even if its magazine is empty. More determined opponents can call the bluff. Players must decide whether to spend a bullet, threaten an enemy or avoid making a confrontation worse. The opponent does not know how much ammunition the protagonist has, so aiming a weapon can sometimes end a confrontation without firing.

cards.heading: Climbing above the toxic dust
cards.text: A cataclysm has left Haventon with ruined buildings and streets covered in toxic dust. The protagonist must climb toward the upper parts of buildings to find breathable air. Descending can offer supplies but exposes him to the dust; climbing uses stamina but provides cleaner air and a view of possible routes. I Am Alive was released on Xbox Live Arcade on March 7, 2012. Its survival systems connect movement through the city with the management of stamina and scarce resources.

main.title: Journey
main.subtitle: Two strangers travel toward a distant mountain
main.summary: Journey lets strangers travel together using musical calls and movement instead of spoken conversation.

cards.heading: Two strangers travel toward a distant mountain
cards.text: Journey allows players to meet another traveller without a spoken introduction or a player name above the figure. A brief musical call can acknowledge the other person, and continuing in the same direction lets the two travel together. The companion is another player making decisions, not a character whose actions have all been scripted.

cards.heading: Landscape and music shape the journey
cards.text: Jenova Chen and the thatgamecompany team built the 2012 PlayStation 3 game around a journey toward a distant mountain. Deserts and a difficult climb provide changing settings for the traveller and a possible companion. The landscape, animation and Austin Wintory's score help shape the emotional progression of the journey.

cards.heading: Communication through calls and movement
cards.text: Without conventional conversation, players communicate through actions the other person can observe. They can wait, return to a companion or continue at a shared pace. A musical call provides another way to acknowledge someone. Two strangers may interpret the same action differently, and moments of help can become a memorable part of their passage toward the mountain.

features.title: Austin Wintory and the music of Journey
features.subtitle: An intimate score for an anonymous adventure
features.summary: Austin Wintory, Tina Guo and the orchestra behind Journey's music.

cards.heading: An intimate score for a vast landscape
cards.text: Austin Wintory spent about three years working on Journey's score. Although the game's distant mountain and heroic journey suggested something grand, he chose an intimate musical approach, with larger passages reserved for particular moments. In his January 2012 account, he described the music as following an emotional transformation. Soloists, including cellist Tina Guo, helped give that music its character.

cards.heading: Travelling alone or with a stranger
cards.text: Journey's creative director Jenova Chen described an anonymous online adventure that players could experience alone or with a stranger. The traveller crosses dunes, ruins and caves towards a mountain. This setting gives the score its context: it accompanies a journey through the landscape and encounters between people, rather than conversations that explain who a companion is or what they are thinking.

cards.heading: Tina Guo and the recording musicians
cards.text: The album credits name Tina Guo on cello, Amy Tatum on flute and bass flute, Charissa Barger on harp, Rodney Wirtz on viola and Noah Gladstone on serpent. Oleg Kontradenko conducted the orchestra in Skopje. Wintory worked from Sony's San Diego studio during the remotely connected recording session. The credits also identify the additional flute of Sara Andon and Lisbeth Scott's vocals in I Was Born for This.

cards.heading: The game and the soundtrack album
cards.text: The composer-hosted Bandcamp edition is dated 19 July 2013 and credits the recording to Sony Computer Entertainment America in 2012. Journey itself was announced for release on 13 March 2012. These dates refer to different publications. The album presents eighteen tracks, from Nascence to I Was Born for This, letting listeners hear the score as a sequence outside the game.

main.title: Kid Icarus: Uprising
main.subtitle: Pit returns after two decades
main.summary: Kid Icarus: Uprising is a 2012 third-person shooter video game developed by Project Sora and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS.

cards.heading: Pit returns after two decades
cards.text: Kid Icarus: Uprising is a 2012 third-person shooter video game developed by Project Sora and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. It is the third installment in the Kid Icarus franchise, the first to be released since Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters in 1991, and the first worldwide release since the original NES game in 1986. It is also the only video game Project Sora made before shutting down in mid-2012.

cards.heading: Aerial battles give way to ground combat
cards.text: Each chapter begins with an on-rails aerial battle, followed by ground exploration and a boss fight. The Circle Pad moves Pit, the stylus or face buttons aim and the L button fires. Waiting between shots charges a stronger attack. On foot, Pit can fight at range or close up, dodge and sprint, with some routes tied to difficulty. Defeat offers another attempt at a lower difficulty and a cost in Hearts, while completing a chapter without dying earns additional rewards.

cards.heading: Sakurai builds a new kind of Kid Icarus
cards.text: Masahiro Sakurai created Uprising after receiving a request from Satoru Iwata to create a launch title for the then in-development Nintendo 3DS. Development began in 2009, but faced multiple difficulties, such as lack of access to the hardware in its early stages, balancing its many elements, and issues with its control scheme. Sakurai was responsible for writing the story, which retained the lighthearted tone of the first Kid Icarus game while having uninterrupted gameplay. A team of composers worked on the music, including Motoi Sakuraba, Yuzo Koshiro, and Yasunori Mitsuda.

main.title: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance
main.subtitle: Two journeys through sleeping worlds
main.summary: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance is Square Enix's Nintendo 3DS action role-playing adventure following Sora and Riku during their Mark of Mastery exam. Their parallel journeys pass through Disney-inspired worlds as they prepare for Master Xehanort's return. The Drop system repeatedly changes which hero the player controls, making both perspectives necessary to progress. Dream Eaters introduce creatures that can become companions as well as enemies. The adventure extends a familiar partnership by placing its members on related paths that have to be understood and completed in turn.

cards.heading: Two journeys through sleeping worlds
cards.text: Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance is Square Enix's Nintendo 3DS action role-playing adventure following Sora and Riku during their Mark of Mastery exam. Their parallel journeys pass through Disney-inspired worlds as they prepare for Master Xehanort's return. The Drop system repeatedly changes which hero the player controls, making both perspectives necessary to progress. Dream Eaters introduce creatures that can become companions as well as enemies. The adventure extends a familiar partnership by placing its members on related paths that have to be understood and completed in turn.

cards.heading: The scenery becomes a way to move
cards.text: Flowmotion lets the characters bounce from walls, spin around poles and travel quickly across the environment. Space becomes something to use during movement and combat rather than only a route between encounters. The Command Deck provides actions, spells and items that can be selected quickly, while world-specific Reality Shifts use touchscreen interactions on certain targets. These additions make the increased emphasis on action concrete. A room can supply a movement opportunity, and an enemy can become the starting point for another short sequence of gestures.

cards.heading: Look after a travelling companion
cards.text: Friendly Dream Eaters called Spirits can be created from collected materials and recruited to assist the heroes. Feeding, petting and playing with them can unlock abilities, connecting a quiet form of care to the next fight. The Drop Gauge meanwhile encourages movement between Sora's and Riku's progress, with bonuses earned for the next period of control. The game joins several kinds of relationship: two heroes sharing an exam, companions growing through attention and familiar fictional worlds offering different events to each traveller. Those connections give its fast movement a longer structure.

main.title: Blacklight: Retribution
main.subtitle: A free-to-play cyberpunk shooter
main.summary: Blacklight: Retribution was a free-to-play first-person shooter video game developed and published by Hardsuit Labs (formerly Zombie Studios) for Microsoft Windows and PlayStation 4.

cards.heading: A free-to-play cyberpunk shooter
cards.text: Blacklight: Retribution was a free-to-play first-person shooter video game developed and published by Hardsuit Labs (formerly Zombie Studios) for Microsoft Windows and PlayStation 4. It was initially published by Perfect World Entertainment on April 3, 2012, with a full Steam release on July 3. A PS4 version was released as a launch title in North America on November 15, 2013, followed by Europe and Australia on December 4.

cards.heading: Weapon depots and the Hyper Reality Visor
cards.text: The sequel to Blacklight: Tango Down, the game is a cyberpunk-themed, arena style shooter that features a number of game modes, including a training mode and others commonly found in games of the same genre. Unique mechanics include weapon depots, which are used to acquire health, ammo, and special weapons, and the Hyper Reality Visor (HRV), which allows players to locate hazards through walls and other obstacles. Completing matches rewards the player with experience and GP, the latter of which can be used to buy additional weapons, armor, and cosmetic items, including skins and tags. Additional game modes were added after its release, including OnSlaught and Siege Mode.

cards.heading: Zombie Studios becomes Hardsuit Labs
cards.text: Retribution saw numerous additions and power shifts throughout its development. Following Zombie's closure in 2015, the remaining team regrouped as Hardsuit Labs, who oversaw development from that point forward. In 2017, Perfect World reverted publishing rights to Hardsuit Labs, who subsequently introduced several new changes, including the migration of US and EU servers.

cards.heading: Reception and the end of online service
cards.text: Blacklight: Retribution received positive reviews from critics, with some calling it an improvement over its predecessor. Praise was directed towards its graphics, mechanics, item balance, and deep customization, while criticism was directed towards its lack of innovation. The game proved popular, achieving one million players within a month of its release. The PC version was discontinued on March 11, 2019 following low user engagement, while the PS4 version was delisted in 2024 and online servers shut down on August 31, 2025.

main.title: Candy Crush Saga
main.subtitle: A Facebook puzzle becomes a mobile phenomenon
main.summary: Candy Crush Saga is a free-to-play tile-matching video game released by King on April 12, 2012, originally for Facebook; other versions for iOS, Android, Windows Phone, and Windows 10 followed.

cards.heading: A Facebook puzzle becomes a mobile phenomenon
cards.text: Candy Crush Saga is a free-to-play tile-matching video game released by King on April 12, 2012, originally for Facebook; other versions for iOS, Android, Windows Phone, and Windows 10 followed. It is a variation of their browser game Candy Crush.

cards.heading: Matching candies within a move limit
cards.text: In the game, players complete levels by swapping colored pieces of candy on a game board to make a match of three or more of the same color, eliminating those candies from the board and replacing them with new ones, which could potentially create further matches. Matches of four or more candies create unique candies that act as power-ups with larger board-clearing abilities. Boards have various goals that must be completed within a fixed number of moves, such as collecting a specific number of a type of candy.

cards.heading: Free-to-play builds a wider series
cards.text:
The game uses a freemium model; while it can be played completely through without spending money, players can buy special actions to help clear more difficult boards, from which King makes its revenues—at its peak, the company was reportedly earning almost $1 million per day. Around 2014, over 93 million people were playing Candy Crush Saga, while revenue over a three-month period as reported by King was over $493 million. Five years after its release on mobile, the Candy Crush Saga series has received over 2.7 billion downloads, and the game has been one of the highest-grossing and most-played mobile apps in that time frame. As of September 2023, it had reached over $20 billion in lifetime revenue, making it one of the highest-grossing media franchises of all time.

King has since released three related titles—Candy Crush Soda Saga, Candy Crush Jelly Saga and Candy Crush Friends Saga—and most of the company's other mobile titles follow the same Saga freemium format.
